title: Telemetry sidecar: trace hooks, enriched logs, and SLO autotriage
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a lightweight telemetry sidecar that attaches trace hooks to inference requests, enriches metrics and logs with request-level context (model, route, customer_tier, kv_cache_hit), and feeds fused signals into SLO autotriage and burn-rate anomaly detectors. This ticket covers the runtime hook API design, a proto sidecar implementation for Hosted/Dedicated agents, the metrics/log enrichment pipeline changes (kafka topic + schema), and initial dashboarding + oncall playbook for automated paging decisions.
background: We frequently see SLO noise and long MTTR when the context that caused latency/error spikes is lost across the runtime, load balancer, and worker processes. Existing trace hooks are fragmented by deployment mode and don't reliably attach model/route/customer metadata. Our goal is a unified, low-overhead mechanism that ensures any span / log / metric can be attributed to a consistent request identity and route metadata so downstream detectors and dashboards can triage automatically.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar exposes a stable trace hook API (attach/detach/context propagation) and is validated with unit tests
Logs and metrics emitted by runtime workers contain consistent request_id, model, route, and customer_tier fields
Enriched telemetry is published to kafka topic rdinf.telemetry.enriched with Avro schema v1 and documented in Confluence
SLO autotriage job consumes fused signal and can produce prioritized incident candidates in staging with >95% precision on top-100 synthetic anomalies
Burn-rate detector evaluates enriched signals and triggers a synthetic alert in staging connected to updated paging policy rules
Dashboard panels for latency-by-route and error-by-model show drilldown links to trace view and enriched log facets
